parts.title: Campus Conversation: Renting a Bicycle
script: Listen to a conversation between a student and a worker at the campus bike shop.
Yes, please. I want to rent a bicycle. My apartment is far from my classes.
Sure. You can rent a bike for a day, a week, or a semester. The semester plan is the cheapest.
It is sixty dollars for the whole semester. A week costs ten dollars.
Then I will take the semester plan. Do I need to bring anything?
Yes. You need to show your student card. You also need to take a helmet. It is free.
Okay. Here is my card. Can I keep the bike at home?
Yes. But please do not leave it outside at night. Use the bike lock that comes with it.
You're welcome. Please bring the bike back on the last day of the semester.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
questions.exp: The student wants to rent a bike.

questions.q: Why does the student want a bike?
o: His apartment is far from his classes
questions.exp: He says his apartment is far from his classes.

questions.q: How much is the semester plan?
Listen again: "Please do not leave it outside at night." Why does the woman say this?
o: To say the helmet is free
questions.exp: She wants him to keep the bike safe, so he should use the lock.

questions.q: What will the student probably do next?
o: Give his student card and take a helmet
questions.exp: She asked for his card and told him to take a helmet.

parts.title: Academic Lecture: How Do Glaciers Form?
script: Listen to part of a lecture in an earth science class.
Today we will talk about glaciers. A glacier is a very large river of ice that moves slowly over land.
Glaciers begin in cold places, like high mountains or places near the North and South Poles. In these places, snow falls every year.
In summer, the snow does not melt completely. So the next winter, new snow falls on top of the old snow.
After many years, the snow becomes heavy. The weight pushes the snow together and turns it into ice.
When the ice is thick enough, gravity pulls it down the mountain. The ice moves very slowly, maybe only a few meters each year.
As a glacier moves, it cuts the rock below it. Over thousands of years, glaciers make deep valleys.
Today, glaciers hold a lot of the fresh water on Earth. But many glaciers are getting smaller because the Earth is getting warmer.
For next class, please read about the biggest glaciers in the world.

questions.q: What is the lecture mainly about?
questions.exp: The professor explains how glaciers form.
They begin in cold places like high mountains or near the Poles.
The weight pushes the snow together into ice.

questions.q: Listen again: "As a glacier moves, it cuts the rock below it." Why does the professor say this?
o: To explain how valleys are made
To talk about a homework test

questions.exp: Only a few meters each year.

o: They are turning into rivers of oil
